_meta.purpose: The routing ratchet. Pins the mapping from advisory LENS names to corpus TAG names, and asserts that a set of real questions can actually be grounded from the corpus. Checked deterministically by build_index.py --check against INDEX.json. No agent runs in the check path.
_meta.why_it_exists: lenses.json routes by LENS name ('terrain-vert', 'hydration-electrolytes', 'race-logistics'). INDEX.json groups by TAG name ('vertical-gain', 'sodium-electrolytes', 'race-prep'). These are two different vocabularies and without a declared mapping between them a grounding node infers it per run. A lens whose tags resolve to zero pages does not fail loudly; it improvises, and its note reads exactly like a grounded one.
_meta.the_underlying_rule: An absent key and an empty list are different failures; so are an unmapped lens and a mapped-but-starved one. Both are made visible here.
_meta.known_gap: Question realism is uneven. These are the questions an ultrarunner actually asks, written from the domain rather than harvested from advisory runs, because this repository has not run one yet. They prove a lens is REACHABLE, not that the corpus answers the question well — depth is not measured here and cannot be without scoring lens output. Nothing in this file grades a page's quality.
_meta.confidentiality: Questions carry nothing about a specific athlete: no weight, no body composition, no health data, no times. A question is a routing probe, not a record of anyone's situation.

lens_tag_map._note: Every lens defined in workflows/lenses.json must appear here, and every tag named must exist in the SCHEMA.md taxonomy. build_index.py checks both directions and additionally asserts that lens_tag_map union unrouted_tags equals the taxonomy EXACTLY — so a new tag cannot enter the taxonomy without someone deciding which of the two it is.

unrouted_tags._note: Taxonomy tags no lens routes to, declared rather than left as an unexplained remainder.
unrouted_tags.failure-modes: cross-cutting — read when hardening any recommendation, not by a single lens
unrouted_tags.coaching-practice: meta — marks a page about who teaches what, not about a training subject
unrouted_tags.framework-comparison: meta — describes a page's form, not its subject
unrouted_tags.best-practices: meta — too broad to route on; every lens would claim it
unrouted_tags.evidence-base: meta — marks that a page carries evidence, not what the evidence is about
unrouted_tags.bibliography: meta — marks a reading lead, not a subject
